fullPassage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.

❌ ③ memory(기억): 잘못된 믿음이 아님
❌ ④ material(자료): 잘못된 믿음과 무관
det.tip: illusion = 착각/잘못된 믿음. a false idea or belief가 핵심

questions.passage: Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after __________ (read) our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 전치사 after 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다 → reading
det.analysis: 전치사 after 뒤에는 명사 역할을 하는 동명사(V-ing)가 와야 한다. read → reading. after reading = 읽은 후에.
det.tip: 전치사(after) + 동명사(reading): after reading our textbook = 교과서를 읽은 후

questions.passage: After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts __________ (disappear). To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: start는 동명사(-ing)를 목적어로 취할 수 있음 → disappearing
det.analysis: 동사 start는 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 취할 수 있으며, 원문은 동명사 형태이다. disappear → disappearing. starts disappearing = 사라지기 시작하다.
det.tip: start + V-ing(동명사): starts disappearing = 사라지기 시작하다

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has __________ the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: nothing to do with=~와 아무 관련이 없는 — 단기 기억은 장기 기억과 무관
det.analysis:
❌ ① everything in common with(~와 모든 것이 공통인): 단기와 장기가 무관하다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② a direct link to(~와 직접적 연결): 무관하다는 맥락과 반대
✅ ③ nothing to do with: 원문 일치. 'this short-term section has ______ the long-term memory'에서 단기 기억 구획은 장기 기억과 아무 관련이 없음 ←정답
❌ ④ a strong resemblance to(~와 강한 유사성): 무관하다는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: have nothing to do with ~ = ~와 아무 관련이 없다

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you __________, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: retest your knowledge=지식을 다시 시험하다 — 그러지 않으면 기억이 사라짐
det.analysis:
❌ ① copy the whole textbook(교과서를 통째로 베끼다): 본문의 자기 시험 강조와 다름
❌ ② read it silently once(한 번 조용히 읽다): 벼락치기식 읽기로 한계가 있음
❌ ③ sleep well every night(매일 잘 자다): 본문과 무관
✅ ④ retest your knowledge: 원문 일치. 'unless you ______, memory vanishes'에서 지식을 다시 시험하지 않으면 기억이 사라짐 ←정답
det.tip: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes
